720	At the top, the connection between the head and the body is
721	the throat. The throat is
722	the connector. It connects the intellectual part with the
723	animal part, the physical part that man shares
724	with the animal, whose whole purpose is simply, technically,
725	to allow a person to exist. That is, thought, seemingly,
726	could exist only in the head, without the body. But then
727	a person could not bring the thought from potential
728	into actuality and carry it out. So the carrying out
729	of thought is in the instruments of action, which are from
730	the shoulders
731	down. Thought happens in the head. What happens in the connection?
732	Speech. The throat and the mouth, that is
733	speech. Speech is this connection.
734	These are the three actions, or three domains of
735	the possibility of
736	human action, and this is an idea that appears in Kabbalah many
737	times: the three fields of action are thought,
738	speech and deed. Deed is the deed of the hands,
739	of the feet, action.
740	Speech is speech,
741	and thought. These are levels, one above
742	the other. Thought is where everything is, that is to say,
743	thought is the most fantastic and most
744	exclusive field, unique to man. Man is able
745	to think, able to understand, able to
746	think. Deed is something man shares with the animals.
747	Many of the deeds we do as human beings
748	we do on an instinctive level, like
749	animals. We are also able to do deeds
750	that are considered, meaning the deed comes after thought
751	first. So there is thought and there is deed. What
752	connects them? The throat,
753	speech. Speech, then, is
754	an amazing tool, unique and exclusive to man. Only human beings
755	speak.
756	I mean intelligent speech. True, dolphins too
757	supposedly speak, and there is also the language of birds, but
758	that is chirping,
759	merely. It is not intelligent speech. Intelligent speech
760	is exclusive, unique to man, and the uniqueness
761	stems from the fact that only man has
762	a soul, a soul in the highest
763	spiritual sense. Therefore the combination of body and soul is expressed
764	in speech. This is what makes speech
765	so enormously important, because, as we said, speech is
766	the garment of
767	thought. If we understand things correctly, we can
768	understand the commandment
769	in the Torah that one must keep
770	one's word: "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep
771	and do." "He shall not profane his word." If a person says something and does not
772	fulfill it, this is called profaning
773	the word. Let us explain this expression for a moment. It appears, by the way,
774	in the Book of Bamidbar, Parashat Matot, in the laws of vows: "If a man
775	vows a vow to HaShem, he shall not profane his word." What does
776	"profane" mean? A word that is not fulfilled is called
777	profaned. Let us explain the word "to profane." What is
778	this
779	profanation? In the previous Parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê,
780	we learned at the end of the Parashah: "If one is found
781	slain, fallen, it is not known who struck him." What is a "chalal"? Look,
782	unfortunately we know this expression
783	all too well from the wars of Israel: "chalalim,"
784	fallen soldiers. What is a "chalal"? Why is a person who died or
785	was killed called
786	a "chalal"? It is also connected to the word
787	"chillul," profanation. Profanation is always the antithesis of
788	sanctification.
789	The profanation of the holy: Shabbat is
790	a holy Shabbat. "Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death."
791	The profanation of Shabbat. Why is it called profanation? The word "chillul"
792	is connected to the word
793	"chalal," empty
794	space. To profane is to take something that has content and remove
795	its content from it.
796	That is called
797	profanation. The people of
798	Israel: when the Holy One, blessed be He, chose us from among all
799	the nations at Mount Sinai, He sent Moshe Rabbeinu
800	and offered us: "You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a
801	holy nation." So I always say jokingly that every Jew
802	is actually a goy, only he has to be a
803	holy goy. "You shall be holy, for I, HaShem, am holy." The people of
804	Israel is a people like all peoples, but it is holy. It has
805	holiness in it. The antithesis of
806	holiness is secularism. By the way, this expression is a shocking
807	expression that we are all used to using, but
808	it is an expression that, for one who understands its meaning, people
809	speak without understanding what they are saying. What does it mean
810	to be a Jew
811	"secular"? "Chiloni" comes from the root "chillul." It
812	comes from the uprooting of holiness. I am a Jew, but I do not
813	do anything holy. I do not keep mitzvot,
814	"who has sanctified us with His commandments." I do not want to be sanctified
815	by His commandments, and I live my life as if I were not
816	a Jew. Now, if a goy lives his life as a non-Jew,
817	fine, he is a goy. But a Jew has
818	the obligation of holiness. When he removes from within himself
819	holiness, he creates
820	an empty space, a profanation. So a person
821	who was killed, murdered, or whose
822	soul departed, an empty space is created, because the central, supreme,
823	spiritual thing that gives him life, "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of
824	life," He gave a breath, a soul of life.
825	The soul gives life to the body. So when this soul
826	departs, an empty space is created. Therefore a person who fell in battle
827	or in general was
828	murdered, not necessarily in battle, as in the Torah: "If one is found
829	slain, fallen in the field, it is not known," it need not
830	be someone who fell in battle, a person from whom his
831	central point has departed, which is
832	the soul. "He shall not profane his word." There is such a thing here too. Speech
833	is holy. Whoever understands what we explained about
834	speech, that speech is the action of the holy soul
835	in the body. Now, the moment the soul acts in the body
836	and intelligent words come out, when a person knows
837	what he
838	committed himself to, it binds him. And if it does not bind
839	him, that is, if he does not stand by it, he does not keep…
